title: Rectify burst token-bucket serialization inconsistency across control plane and runtime
creator: Maya Chen
description: Multiple customers (hosted and dedicated) reported intermittent opaque 429s and long tail latency spikes after a routine control-plane deploy. Investigation shows a deterministic mismatch in how burst token-bucket state was serialized by the control plane and how the runtime deserialized it during token reconciliation. The mismatch appears only when burst state contains a fractional refill timestamp and under certain replication lag between control-plane replicas, resulting in negative effective tokens and immediate enforced throttling for affected tenants. Private customers with older runtime versions saw similar behavior when exposed to a control-plane variant producing the new serialization format.

root_cause: A non-backwards-compatible change to the burst token-bucket serialization introduced fractional refill timestamps. Under replication lag and version skew, control plane published burst states with sub-second fractional values which the runtime deserializer interpreted incorrectly (floating point rounding to a negative small number). This produced negative available token counts which the throttler treated as immediate exhaustion and returned 429s. Private deployments running older runtimes were susceptible when the control plane sent the new format.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy control-plane variant with fractional-timestamp serialization enabled
Introduce a replication delay between control-plane replicas (simulate by pausing one replica for ~200ms)
Publish a tenant burst update with a partial-second refill time
Observe runtime deserialization: token count becomes negative and subsequent requests receive 429s until reconciliation
Reproducible in both hosted and dedicated stacks; for private customers, reproduce by pointing runtime to an updated control-plane snapshot
temporary_mitigation: Normalize burst token count to Math.max(0, computed_tokens) in the runtime deserialization layer (hotfix deployed to all regions)
Control-plane guard to strip fractional component of refill timestamps until full fix in place
Scoped rollback of the control-plane change where applicable for Private customers on request
Customer-facing communication and temporary quota increases for impacted tenants while mitigation is active
fix_plan: PR #6123 - Add versioned serialization envelope and tolerance checks for fractional timestamps: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6123
PR #6127 - Add reconciliation job that replays last known-good burst state and emits audit events: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/6127
Add unit tests for cross-version serialization/deserialization and property-based tests for edge-case timestamps
Backport stable serialization patch to runtime-1.18 and runtime-1.19 branches for private/Dedicated customers still on earlier releases
qa_and_rollout: Canary rollout to 5% of traffic in us-west2 (monitored for 48h) - started 2026-02-22
Expanded canary to 20% after 24h with zero recurrence
Full rollout in controlled waves across regions over 72h with rollback monitoring hooks
Add synthetic canary that intentionally publishes fractional burst timestamps to ensure deserializer tolerates them
E2E tests added to CI that run cross-version serialization checks during merge
follow_up_actions: Add schema version header to burst-state pub/sub messages to enforce forward/backward compatibility
Implement periodic reconciliation and an eventual consistency auditor that alerts on negative token counts
Update operator runbook and incident playbook to include this class of serialization mismatch
Customer outreach checklist: list of impacted tenants, timeline of events, and remediation steps
Schedule a postmortem writeup and distribution to GTM/Support (due 2026-03-03)
